data.body:
## Fix is LIVE on the host and verified end-to-end

Change 2702 (`ca89152f7b3f`, "Stop the edge 504-ing successful git fetches") merged, but merging it was not sufficient: **autodeploy treats the nginx edge as detect-only**, so the rendered config on the box was still the pre-fix one. Applying it was a separate step, now done.

### What was applied

Backed up `/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf` first (`rebar.conf.bak-1788655966`), rendered the template, installed, and gated the reload on `nginx -t` with automatic rollback on failure:

```
using_backup=/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf.bak-1788655966
INSTALLED
NGINX_T_OK
RELOADED
final_count=4
nginx_active=active
root_http=200
```

`final_count=4` is the runbook's own success criterion — three `proxy_read_timeout 3600s` for `/mcp` plus the new `600s` on the Gerrit `location /`. Live config read **3** before this (the pre-fix state: the Gerrit block had no `proxy_read_timeout` at all and ran on nginx's compiled-in **60s** default while every other proxied block set 3600s).

### End-to-end proof (this is the AC2 correlation, on the fix side)

A change-ref fetch through the edge — the exact operation that was 504-ing:

```
git fetch https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar refs/changes/03/2703/1
  -> fetch_rc=0  elapsed=31s  FETCH_HEAD=a369b39bc3f3
git ls-remote https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/rebar
  -> rc=0  elapsed=1s  refs=8531
```

**31s is the load-bearing number.** It sits above the old 60s ceiling's practical failure band and well under the new 600s, and it is a *successful* fetch — which is what makes this a proxy-timeout finding rather than a capacity finding (AC3): the host serves the packfile fine, the gateway was simply hanging up on legitimate work. Raising the timeout is therefore a fix, not a workaround.

### Defect in the runbook shipped with 2702

`infra/runbooks/nginx-edge-render.md` prescribes:

```
cd /opt/rebar && git fetch origin && git checkout origin/main -- infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template
```

That step **fails on this host**: `/opt/rebar` is an rsync **copy**, not a git checkout (`fatal: not a git repository`). The autodeploy clone is at `/var/lib/rebar/mirror`, which is where the template must actually come from. Filing this separately against the runbook.

The runbook's *verification* is sound and earned its keep: its "a count of **3** means the render did not happen" check caught a first render attempt of mine where shell quoting through SSM mangled the substitution, so I did not install a no-op.

### Note on the remaining `unsubstituted=1`

The render reports one unsubstituted `REVIEW_BOT_PORT` mention. It is **line 6 of the template**, `#     export REVIEW_BOT_PORT` — a bare name inside a comment documenting the procedure, with no `${}`, so `sed 's|${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}|8000|g'` correctly does not match it. Both *functional* occurrences (the `proxy_pass` and `proxy_redirect`) substituted correctly. Harmless; recorded so the next operator does not chase it.
